tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.caption: The oracle answers every question put to it, which is a different skill from answering the question you meant.
tools.desc: OpenAI's general-purpose AI chatbot, handles writing, coding, research, and image generation in one conversation.
tools.fact: Became one of the fastest-growing consumer apps in history after its 2022 launch.
tools.why: The realm's most popular familiar for a reason: a strong free tier, does nearly everything, and anyone can use it on day one.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.caption: The palace already has a bard, a scribe, a cook, and a guard captain. Now it has an oracle standing behind all four at once.
tools.desc: Google's AI assistant, deeply integrated across Search, Docs, Gmail, and Android.
tools.fact: Natively understands images, video, and audio in the same conversation, not just text.
tools.why: Free, capable, and already living inside your Gmail and Docs. The home-field advantage is real.

tools.name: Gemini Notebook
tools.caption: The scholar read only the books you gave him, yet spoke with the confidence of a man who'd read every book in the world.
tools.desc: Google's source-grounded AI notebook, renamed from NotebookLM in July 2026; the free tier covers 100 notebooks and 50 chats a day.
tools.fact: Refuses to answer from general knowledge, every response is grounded in the documents you actually upload.
tools.why: Free, grounded in your own sources, and hard to make hallucinate. The best-value scholar in the entire realm.

tools.name: Claude
tools.caption: One scribe reads the entire library before answering, and the line to ask it anything now stretches out the door.
tools.desc: Anthropic's AI assistant, built with a focus on careful reasoning and long-context conversations.
tools.fact: Can hold entire books or codebases in a single conversation thanks to its large context window.
tools.why: A careful, well-read scholar with a strong free tier. Loses a hair to ChatGPT only on sheer breadth of extra gadgets.

tools.name: DeepSeek
tools.caption: A traveling scholar arrives from a distant kingdom, gives away free lessons, and every local tutor suddenly discovers competitive pricing.
tools.desc: An AI lab's chatbot that rivals top models while publishing its models with open weights.
tools.fact: Its models can be downloaded and run by anyone, not just accessed through a paid API.
tools.why: Top-tier brains for free, with open weights for anyone who wants to run the spell at home. Hard to beat on value.

tools.name: Canva Magic Studio
tools.caption: Give a village a thousand magic paintbrushes and you get a thousand banners that all look the same.
tools.desc: AI design tools bundled into Canva Pro, from ~$10-15/month.
tools.fact: The current #1-ranked tool on Solos Gems, across all 51 tools reviewed.
tools.why: Rolled high on value, ease, and a free tier generous enough to feel like a trap. It isn't. The fanciest spells just live behind Pro.

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.caption: The scribe took perfect notes on a meeting that never needed to happen.
tools.desc: Meeting transcription with unlimited minutes on every tier, including free.
tools.fact: Unlimited transcription minutes even on its free plan, unusual for the category.
tools.why: Unlimited transcription on every tier, free included, is the kind of loot drop that makes the rest of the meeting-notes guild look stingy.

tools.name: CapCut
tools.caption: Every apprentice bard gets the same enchanted editing quill for free, and the entire market square starts sounding suspiciously polished overnight.
tools.desc: ByteDance's free AI-powered video editor, built around fast short-form editing for social platforms.
tools.fact: Became one of the most-used video editing apps in the world largely through organic use by short-form creators.
tools.why: A free, powerful editor with AI tricks built for short-form video. Hard to beat for social creators.

tools.name: Fathom
tools.caption: A scribe sits in on every council meeting for free and somehow never bills the treasury for a single scroll.
tools.desc: A free AI meeting recorder that transcribes, summarizes, and highlights action items automatically.
tools.fact: Acquired by Superhuman in September 2026; its free plan, which has no cap on recorded minutes, carried on unchanged.
tools.why: A free meeting recorder with good summaries and no fuss. One of the best free spells in the realm.

tools.name: DeepL
tools.caption: The translator scroll gets the idiom right more often than the scholars who spent a decade studying it, which nobody in the department likes to admit out loud.
tools.desc: AI translation widely regarded as the accuracy leader for European languages.
tools.fact: Frequently outperforms larger general-purpose AI models on nuanced, idiomatic translation quality.
tools.why: The translator many call the most accurate in the realm, with a strong free tier. A polyglot familiar.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.caption: The apprentice finishes your sentence before you do, which is either flattering or the reason you've stopped finishing your own sentences.
tools.desc: GitHub's AI pair programmer, built directly into your code editor.
tools.fact: One of the earliest mainstream AI coding tools, it helped popularize AI-assisted programming as a category.
tools.why: The default coding familiar, with a free tier and editor integration everywhere. Hard to go wrong.

tools.name: Cal.com
tools.caption: The open-source appointment book that answers the castle bell and books your meetings for you, all on the free plan.
tools.desc: An open-source Calendly alternative with AI-assisted routing forms and an AI phone agent, Cal.ai, that can take calls and book meetings on your behalf.
tools.fact: The free plan already includes routing forms, workflow automation, and Cal.ai phone agent features, most competitors gate all three behind a paid tier.
tools.why: An open-source Calendly rival with a generous free plan and an AI phone agent. Better value than the original.

tools.name: Google Stitch
tools.caption: The tailor sketches five matching outfits from one mumbled description, then hands you the pattern so the other tailor can take the credit.
tools.desc: A free Google Labs tool that turns a prompt, sketch, or voice description into multi-screen app and web UI designs, exportable to Figma or code.
tools.fact: There is no paid tier at all. It runs on a daily credit allowance, and designs paste straight into Figma as editable layers.
tools.why: Free multi-screen UI designs that paste straight into Figma. Hard to argue with free and good.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.caption: The guild doesn't sell the golem separately. It just shows up with your tavern membership and asks where the bugs are.
tools.desc: OpenAI's coding agent, bundled into every ChatGPT plan including Free, that builds features, fixes bugs, and proposes pull requests in the cloud or your terminal.
tools.fact: There is no separate Codex subscription. It rides along with ChatGPT, though the command-line version starts at the $20/month Plus plan.
tools.why: A strong coding agent bundled into ChatGPT plans, free included. Excellent value if you already pay for ChatGPT.

tools.name: Google Antigravity
tools.caption: Hiring five apprentices at once sounded efficient right up until you became the full-time manager of five apprentices.
tools.desc: Google's agent-first development platform where you hand coding tasks to AI agents that plan, build, and test in a browser. Free for individual developers.
tools.fact: Works as a command center for several local agents at once, with scheduled messages so an agent can pick up work while you sleep.
tools.why: Free for individuals and runs a whole party of coding agents. Powerful, still new, and a little overwhelming.

tools.name: Kling AI
tools.caption: The illusion of motion gets more convincing every season, and the free trial keeps getting more generous, which never quite feels like it should both be true.
tools.desc: A video generator known for realistic motion and a generous free tier.
tools.fact: Its Omni mode can lip-sync two different characters in one scene, each mouth matched to its own audio track.
tools.why: Realistic motion and a generous free tier. One of the best values in AI video right now.

tools.name: Dreamina
tools.caption: The illusionist's workshop gives out free tokens every morning, which is either generous or exactly how they get you hooked on illusions.
tools.desc: CapCut's AI studio for images, short videos, and talking avatars from text, photos, or audio, with free daily credits and low-cost paid plans.
tools.fact: Bundles ByteDance's Seedance video model and Seedream image model in one place, so you don't hop between tools.
tools.why: Free daily credits, strong video and image models, and cheap upgrades. One of the best deals in AI video.

tools.name: Kimi
tools.caption: The scholar from the moon kingdom reads your entire library before breakfast, then politely asks if there's a second library.
tools.desc: Moonshot AI's assistant, built around its K3 model for agentic coding and knowledge work, with deep research and scheduled tasks.
tools.fact: Made its name on very long context, reading whole stacks of documents in a single conversation.
tools.why: Free, reads a whole library in one sitting, and handles agentic tasks well. A strong assistant most of the realm hasn't met yet.

tools.name: Linear
tools.caption: Every quest board in the kingdom used to be scrawled notes and thumbtacks. Someone finally built one that closes the note for you the moment the quest is actually done.
tools.desc: A fast, keyboard-driven issue tracker for software teams with AI-assisted triage and summaries, genuinely free for small teams up to 250 issues, Basic $10/user/month.
tools.fact: The free plan caps at 250 open issues rather than a time limit or seat count, so a small team can stay on it indefinitely as long as it keeps closing tickets.
tools.why: A fast, beautiful issue tracker, free for small teams. Makes project management feel almost pleasant.

tools.name: Qwen Chat
tools.caption: The eastern kingdom's oracle answers for free and hands copies of its spellbook to anyone who asks. The other kingdoms find this rude.
tools.desc: Alibaba's free AI assistant built on its Qwen models, which are also released with open weights for anyone to run.
tools.fact: The Qwen model family is among the most widely downloaded open-weight models, used as the base for countless other AI projects.
tools.why: Free to use and backed by open-weight models anyone can run. Strong value, a little less polish than the household names.

tools.name: Raycast
tools.caption: The spellbook opens with two keys, remembers every spell you've ever cast, and comes with a familiar who can see what you're looking at.
tools.desc: A free launcher for apps, clipboard history, windows, and snippets, with Raycast AI chat and commands on Pro from $10/month.
tools.fact: Screen awareness lets the AI read what is on your screen right now, so you can ask about it without copying and pasting.
tools.why: A free launcher that makes your whole computer faster, with AI on Pro. Beloved for good reason.

tools.name: Meta AI
tools.caption: The tavern owner installs a fortune teller at every table for free, and asks nothing in return except your undivided attention.
tools.desc: Meta's free AI assistant, built directly into Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, and Messenger.
tools.fact: Runs inside the messaging apps billions of people already have open, no separate app required.
tools.why: Free and already in your group chats. Convenient as a tavern bard, not the deepest thinker in the room.

tools.name: Hailuo AI
tools.caption: One portrait, one spell, and suddenly your grandfather is skydiving. Nobody asked how the illusionist got hold of the painting.
tools.desc: MiniMax's AI video, image, and audio generator, best known for turning a single photo into a short animated clip.
tools.fact: Its Omni Reference feature steers a generation with your own photos and notes, and you can earn extra free credits by answering surveys.
tools.why: Strong video from a photo or prompt with free credits to burn. A rising star of the video guild.

tools.name: MagicSchool AI
tools.caption: One overworked teacher is handed a whole staff room's worth of lesson plans, rubrics, and polite emails to angry parents, all before first bell.
tools.desc: An AI toolkit built for teachers, covering lesson plans, rubrics, feedback, and classroom communication.
tools.fact: Its free tier includes more usable tools than many competing paid education platforms.
tools.why: A free toolkit that saves teachers hours on lesson plans and rubrics. A paladin for the classroom.

tools.name: Napkin AI
tools.caption: The cartographer listens to your rambling explanation once, then hands you a map that makes you sound like you knew what you meant all along.
tools.desc: Turns plain text into diagrams, flowcharts, infographics, and mind maps you can edit. Free plan with weekly credits, Plus from $9/month.
tools.fact: Paste a paragraph and it offers several visual layouts for the same idea, so you pick a diagram instead of drawing one.
tools.why: Free weekly credits and turns walls of text into clean diagrams in seconds. A narrow trick, performed beautifully.

tools.name: Buffer
tools.caption: The town crier finally gets a scheduling scroll so the announcements go out at dawn without anyone actually waking up at dawn.
tools.desc: Social media scheduling and analytics with a genuinely usable free tier for solo creators.
tools.fact: Built from the start for individual creators and small teams rather than enterprise social war rooms.
tools.why: Social scheduling with a genuinely usable free tier. The easiest way to post everywhere without losing your mind.

tools.name: Khanmigo
tools.caption: A tutor that refuses to just hand you the answer, insisting instead on walking beside you while you get there the slow, correct way.
tools.desc: Khan Academy's AI tutor, free for teachers and low-cost for families, built to guide rather than give answers.
tools.fact: Acts as a Socratic tutor across math, science, and test prep, prompting students toward the answer instead of stating it.
tools.why: A free, patient tutor for teachers and cheap for families that refuses to just hand over answers. Wholesome and effective.

tools.name: Granola
tools.caption: Nobody saw the scribe come in. By the time the council adjourned, the minutes were already perfect.
tools.desc: An AI notetaker that runs on your desktop and never joins the call as a visible bot.
tools.fact: Builds its notes from your own rough, typed scribbles during the meeting, not just a raw transcript.
tools.why: The notetaker with no bot at the table. Easy, clever, and loved by everyone who tries it.

tools.name: Beehiiv
tools.caption: The town crier now competes with forty other criers yelling different news in the same square.
tools.desc: Newsletter platform built for monetization from day one; 0% commission on paid subscriptions.
tools.fact: Takes 0% commission on paid subscriptions, unlike most newsletter platforms.
tools.why: Zero commission on paid subscriptions from day one. The newsletter guild's only innkeeper who doesn't skim off the top of your tips.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.caption: The owl corrected every letter in the kingdom's mail and somehow made everyone sound like the owl.
tools.desc: Grammar, tone, and clarity checking everywhere you write.
tools.fact: Checks writing inside almost any app on your device, not just its own editor.
tools.why: So easy you forget it's casting. The free tier alone saves more embarrassing emails than most paid tools.

tools.name: Consensus
tools.caption: Instead of one scholar's opinion, you get a little meter showing how much the entire scholarly guild actually agrees, which is somehow more useful and more damning.
tools.desc: An AI search engine that answers questions using evidence from peer-reviewed research papers.
tools.fact: Shows a visual 'Consensus Meter' indicating how much scientific agreement exists on a given question.
tools.why: Answers backed by peer-reviewed papers, with a free tier. A scholar who cites real sources.

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.caption: The castle's steward now whispers suggestions into every room at once: the study, the kitchen, the war table, the outhouse.
tools.desc: Microsoft's AI assistant woven directly into Word, Excel, Outlook, and Windows itself.
tools.fact: Can see and act on what's already open on your screen inside Microsoft 365 apps.
tools.why: Free, useful, and woven through Windows and Office. The deep Office magic costs extra gold.

tools.name: Superwhisper
tools.caption: Speak into the void and the words appear typed in whatever scroll you happen to be holding, running entirely on the wizard's own tower instead of someone else's.
tools.desc: AI voice dictation for Mac and iOS that types in any app, running on local AI models, free or $8.49/month for cloud models and file transcription.
tools.fact: Runs entirely on-device using local AI models, so the free tier works offline with no word cap and no account required.
tools.why: Private, on-device dictation for Mac and iOS, free to start. A quiet, loyal scribe.

tools.name: Zed
tools.caption: A blacksmith forges the fastest quill in the land and hands it out for free. The enchantment that makes it whisper answers back costs extra.
tools.desc: A fast, Rust-built code editor with real-time collaboration and optional AI features, the editor itself is free forever, Pro adds unlimited AI edit predictions for $10/month.
tools.fact: The base editor never requires a subscription at all, you only pay if you want Zed's own hosted AI models instead of bringing your own API key.
tools.why: A blazing-fast free editor with optional AI. Lean and lovely, with fewer AI tricks than the heavyweights.

tools.name: Photoroom
tools.caption: Every merchant's wares now float in the same empty white nowhere, all origin scrubbed away for the sale.
tools.desc: AI background removal and product photo editing, from $7.50/month billed yearly.
tools.fact: Purpose-built for e-commerce product photos rather than general design work.
tools.why: Background removal so quick and cheap it feels like a cantrip. The top product-photo tool for small sellers.

tools.name: Wispr Flow
tools.caption: The scribe transcribed every stammer, every um, every change of mind, faithfully, exactly as spoken, which turned out to be the problem.
tools.desc: AI voice dictation that writes in your own tone across any app on your computer, free or $12/user/month.
tools.fact: Works system-wide, not just inside one app, so it dictates into email, Slack, or a code editor alike.
tools.why: Talk and it types, cleanly, in any app. Easy, generous free use, and genuinely faster than your fingers.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.caption: One great bazaar where every wizard in every kingdom leaves their spellbooks out for anyone to copy, no toll, no questions, occasional chaos.
tools.desc: The largest hub for open-source AI models, datasets, and demo spaces.
tools.fact: Hosts well over a million public models and datasets, most of it free to download and run.
tools.why: The great open library of models, mostly free. Indispensable for builders, bewildering for everyone else.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.caption: Every wizard's illusion has been beautiful and unreadable for years. One wizard finally figures out how to make the banner say what the banner is supposed to say.
tools.desc: An AI image generator that specializes in getting readable text inside the image right.
tools.fact: Reaches roughly 90% accuracy rendering legible text and logos inside generated images, long a weak spot for image models.
tools.why: The rare image wizard that can actually spell. A free tier and readable text make it a designer's friend.

tools.name: Perplexity Comet
tools.caption: The scrying mirror now walks around with you, reading over your shoulder and occasionally grabbing the quill out of your hand.
tools.desc: Perplexity's AI-native web browser that reads, researches, and can act on the page you're viewing.
tools.fact: Free for all Perplexity account holders, unusual for a browser built around a paid AI subscription product.
tools.why: A free AI browser that reads and acts on the page you're on. Strong agent tricks, still settling in.

tools.name: Dia
tools.caption: The new carriage comes with a talking horse that has read every tab you left open, and it has opinions about all forty-seven.
tools.desc: The Browser Company's AI browser for work. It chats with your open tabs and pulls together info from your other tools. Free on Mac and Windows.
tools.fact: Its Morning Brief gathers your calendar, inbox, and key links into one page before the workday starts.
tools.why: A free AI browser that actually understands your tabs. Promising, young, and still earning its reputation.

tools.name: Julius
tools.caption: Hand a scholar your whole ledger and it doesn't just read the numbers back, it draws you a chart of exactly how bad they are.
tools.desc: An AI data analyst you chat with, upload a spreadsheet or database and it writes and runs the code to clean, analyze, and chart it. Free plan available, Plus from $16/month annual.
tools.fact: Every plan runs on a monthly credit grant instead of a message cap, so one complex multi-step analysis can burn through a lot more allowance than a single quick chart request.
tools.why: Chat with your spreadsheet and it builds the charts. A free plan and a gentle learning curve make it a top analyst.

tools.name: Mistral Vibe
tools.caption: One kingdom's oracle refuses to write down anything it hears. The neighboring kingdoms find this suspicious and also deeply relaxing.
tools.desc: Mistral AI's assistant, renamed from Le Chat in May 2026, now pairing a work chatbot with a coding agent. Free plan, Pro from $14.99/month.
tools.fact: Remembers details from conversations weeks earlier, even on the free tier.
tools.why: A solid free assistant now doubling as a coding agent. A strong choice if you'd rather not hand your scrolls to the usual giants.

tools.name: QuillBot
tools.caption: The same scribe that rewrites your scroll for clarity will also, if asked nicely, tell you whether a rival's scroll was ghostwritten.
tools.desc: A paraphrasing and grammar tool that also includes a free AI detector and plagiarism checker.
tools.fact: Started purely as a paraphrasing tool before expanding into detection as AI-written text became common to check for.
tools.why: Paraphrasing, grammar, and a free AI detector in one cheap pouch. Not glamorous, very useful.

tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.caption: The otter wrote down every word spoken in the war council, perfectly, and still couldn't tell you who won.
tools.desc: Real-time meeting transcription and summaries; Business tier bills a 5-seat minimum.
tools.fact: Can join a call automatically and start transcribing without anyone manually starting a recorder.
tools.why: A reliable court scribe with fast notes, docked a few points because the Business tier sells seats in packs of five like a wizard bulk-buying candles.

tools.name: Reclaim.ai
tools.caption: The guard who stands between you and the next meeting was hired by you, to stop you.
tools.desc: An AI calendar tool that auto-schedules habits, focus time, and tasks around your existing meetings, with a genuinely free tier for a single calendar.
tools.fact: Automatically defends time for recurring habits like exercise or deep work, rescheduling them itself the moment a meeting collides.
tools.why: Defends your focus time like a loyal shield-bearer, with a free tier that actually covers a solo calendar.

tools.name: Flux
tools.caption: A new forge opens outside the old masters' guild, makes photorealistic weapons just as sharp, and immediately every rival forge starts benchmarking against it.
tools.desc: A photorealism-focused image generation model from Black Forest Labs.
tools.fact: Built by former Stable Diffusion researchers, it's become a common benchmark for photorealistic AI image quality.
tools.why: Gorgeous photorealism with open-weight versions you can run yourself. Top-tier art, a bit fiddly to wield.

tools.name: Cline
tools.caption: The guild's free apprentice will work with any wizard's spells you hand it. It just asks that you pay the wizards yourself.
tools.desc: An open-source AI coding agent for VS Code and the command line. The tool is free; you pay only for the AI model usage, with your own API keys or Cline's.
tools.fact: Works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, and more, so you can switch models without switching tools.
tools.why: Free, open source, and no vendor lock-in. Model costs are on you, and it assumes you're comfortable reading code.

tools.name: Devin Desktop
tools.caption: The apprentice now takes the whole quest, not just the next line of the scroll, and checks back with you before doing anything truly reckless.
tools.desc: Cognition's AI code editor, renamed from Windsurf in June 2026, where the Devin Local agent handles multi-step coding tasks while you stay in the loop.
tools.fact: Now owned by Cognition, the same company behind the autonomous coding agent Devin.
tools.why: A capable agentic code editor with a free tier. A real rival to Cursor, with a bumpier ownership history.

tools.name: Udio
tools.caption: A full song, with separate tracks and a coherent chorus, appears from a written description, and somewhere a bard quietly updates their resume.
tools.desc: AI music generation known for coherent full songs with mixed, separable tracks.
tools.fact: Exports separate vocal, drum, bass, and instrument stems so you can remix the output in real music software.
tools.why: Coherent songs with separable tracks and a free tier. A serious rival to Suno.

tools.name: Auphonic
tools.caption: The bard's uneven lute playing gets leveled out automatically, so the recording sounds like one performance instead of three different volumes arguing.
tools.desc: AI audio post-production that automatically levels, cleans up noise, and masters podcast episodes.
tools.fact: Normalizes multiple speakers recorded at different volumes into one consistent, broadcast-ready level automatically.
tools.why: Levels and cleans podcast audio automatically, with free monthly hours. Quietly essential.

tools.name: Character.AI
tools.caption: The tavern where every NPC talks back. Wildly popular, and the innkeeper now checks IDs at the door.
tools.desc: Chat and roleplay with AI characters, or create your own. Free to use, with c.ai+ at $9.99/month. Open-ended chat has been adults-only since November 2025.
tools.fact: Removed open-ended chat for users under 18 in November 2025, leaving teens with story and creation tools instead.
tools.why: Free and endlessly entertaining for roleplay and storytelling. Not built for real work, and safety concerns have reshaped it.

tools.name: Raphael AI
tools.caption: A tavern portrait painter who works for free all night, so long as you wait in line and let him stamp his signature across every canvas.
tools.desc: Web AI image generator that lets you start without signing up; free images carry a watermark, paid Pro, Ultimate and Max plans remove it.
tools.fact: Signed-in free users get unlimited generations in basic mode (with a short queue) and up to 4 images per prompt.
tools.why: Wander in with no account and draw all night, though the watermark and the queue are the toll at the gate.

tools.name: tl;dv
tools.caption: Nobody at the table notices the owl in the rafters until the minutes get read back verbatim.
tools.desc: An AI meeting recorder and transcription tool for Zoom, Meet, and Teams with unlimited free recordings and 10 free AI summaries a month before paid plans start at $18/user/month.
tools.fact: The free plan's recording and transcription limits are genuinely unlimited, the only real cap is on AI-generated meeting summaries, most competitors throttle recording itself.
tools.why: Unlimited free recording and transcription. The only real cap is on AI summaries, which is a fair trade.

tools.name: Veo
tools.caption: The royal court's own illusionist joins the family of scrying tools already crowding the palace, in case the other three weren't enough.
tools.desc: Google's AI video generation model, built into Gemini and Google's creative tools.
tools.fact: Frequently cited as one of the top overall picks for AI video quality among current models.
tools.why: Google's top-tier video with sound, built into Gemini. Best results need a paid plan.

tools.name: Cartesia
tools.caption: The messenger replies before you finish your sentence, which is impressive and also exactly what your rudest uncle does.
tools.desc: Real-time voice AI: Sonic text-to-speech, Ink speech-to-text, and phone voice agents. Free plan, Pro from $5/month.
tools.fact: Built for very low latency, so voice agents answer fast enough to feel like a conversation instead of a walkie-talkie.
tools.why: Ultra-fast voice AI with a free plan and a $5 Pro tier. A builder's delight, a little technical for others.

tools.name: Elicit
tools.caption: Extracting the one useful sentence from four hundred research papers used to take a semester. Now it takes an afternoon and a very specific request.
tools.desc: An AI research assistant built for systematic literature reviews and evidence extraction.
tools.fact: Can pull structured data out of hundreds of academic papers at once instead of you reading each one manually.
tools.why: Automates literature reviews and evidence extraction, free to start. Superb for researchers.

tools.name: n8n
tools.caption: Someone finally wired every guild hall in the city together with string and pulleys, free for anyone willing to learn where the string goes.
tools.desc: An open-source workflow automation platform that connects hundreds of apps together.
tools.fact: Because it's open-source, you can self-host it for free instead of paying per task.
tools.why: Open source and self-hostable, so the gold cost can hit zero. The price is your time learning the spellbook.

tools.name: Krea AI
tools.caption: You sketch three rough lines and the illusion finishes the painting before your hand leaves the parchment, which is either delightful or deeply unsettling.
tools.desc: Real-time AI image generation and upscaling, showing results as you sketch or adjust the prompt.
tools.fact: Updates the generated image live as you draw or type, instead of waiting for a full render each time.
tools.why: Images that update live as you sketch, plus a free tier. Delightful to play with, genuinely useful too.

tools.name: Moises
tools.caption: The bard's apprentice can pull the drummer clean out of any song, which is great for practice and terrible news for the drummer.
tools.desc: Splits any song into separate vocals, drums, bass, guitar, and more for practice and remixing, plus chord detection and tempo control. Free plan with monthly upload limits.
tools.fact: Moises Studio lets bandmates arrange and record the same session together in a browser in real time, no installs or file swapping.
tools.why: Stem separation good enough for working musicians, with a usable free tier. A practice-room essential.

tools.name: Stable Diffusion
tools.caption: One wizard publishes the entire spellbook for free, and now every apprentice in every basement is casting the same illusion with their own personal twist.
tools.desc: An open-weight image generation model that anyone can download, run locally, and fine-tune.
tools.fact: Because it's open-weight, it spawned an entire ecosystem of community fine-tunes and tools built on top of it.
tools.why: Free and open to run on your own machine forever. Unbeatable value, if you can survive the setup dungeon.

tools.name: Warp
tools.caption: The dungeon's command line finally hired a guide who knows the way, and you can even pay the guide with your own gold.
tools.desc: An AI-native terminal that pairs a fast, GPU-rendered shell with an agent mode that can plan and run multi-step coding tasks directly in your command line.
tools.fact: Free users can bring their own OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google API key instead of paying for Warp's own AI credits.
tools.why: A fast terminal with a capable agent mode and a free tier. Makes the command line feel less like a dungeon.

tools.name: Amazon Q Developer
tools.caption: The cloud kingdom hires its own royal engineer to explain the cloud kingdom's own plumbing back to you, in exchange for rent.
tools.desc: AWS's AI coding assistant for writing, transforming, and security-scanning code inside supported IDEs, free for individuals with 50 agentic requests a month, Pro $19/user/month.
tools.fact: AWS is retiring Q Developer's IDE plugins and paid subscriptions in favor of a successor tool called Kiro, new signups already closed as of mid-2026.
tools.why: Free for individuals and great at AWS plumbing. Less exciting outside the AWS kingdom.

tools.name: Willow Voice
tools.caption: The dictation quill learns your particular phrasing over time, so the scroll starts sounding more like you and less like a very polite stranger.
tools.desc: Cross-platform AI dictation for Mac, Windows, and iOS with style memory that learns how you write, from a free tier of 2,000 words a week up to $15/month for unlimited use.
tools.fact: Its iPhone keyboard now ships with free, unlimited AI dictation built in, a rare case of a paid tool's core feature going free on mobile.
tools.why: Cross-platform dictation that learns how you write, with a free tier. A friendly rival to Wispr Flow.

tools.name: Rows
tools.caption: The abacus grew opinions. It now argues with you about what the numbers mean, in the same box where you typed them.
tools.desc: A spreadsheet built with AI formulas and live data connectors baked in from the start.
tools.fact: Can pull live data directly from APIs and other apps into a cell, instead of a manual copy-paste import.
tools.why: A spreadsheet with AI and live data built in, plus a real free plan. Quietly excellent.

tools.name: Shopify Magic
tools.caption: Every shopkeeper in the bazaar is handed a ghostwriter for their signs, and the signs all start sounding suspiciously enthusiastic.
tools.desc: AI features built directly into Shopify: product descriptions, email content, and image editing.
tools.fact: Included at no extra cost inside every Shopify plan, rather than sold as a separate add-on.
tools.why: Free AI inside Shopify for descriptions and images. Only useful if you already live in Shopify's castle.

tools.name: Rytr
tools.caption: A budget scribe who'll happily draft the tavern's flyer, the merchant's email, and the guild's social post, all for less than the cost of real parchment.
tools.desc: A budget AI writing assistant covering short-form marketing copy, emails, and social posts.
tools.fact: Its free plan supports a genuinely usable monthly character allowance, not just a one-time trial.
tools.why: A cheap, cheerful copywriter with a free plan. Not deep, very affordable.

tools.name: Descript
tools.caption: Cutting the word from the scroll doesn't stop the bard from having said it out loud in the tavern.
tools.desc: Edit audio/video by editing a text transcript.
tools.fact: Deleting a word from the transcript deletes it from the actual audio and video too.
tools.why: Editing video by editing text is a legendary spell. The learning curve and price keep it from the top of the tower.

tools.name: Airtable
tools.caption: Every civilization eventually invents a way to sort things it will never look at again.
tools.desc: A spreadsheet-database hybrid with AI credits for generating interfaces and automations from your own data.
tools.fact: The free tier (1,000 records/base, 500 AI credits/editor) genuinely covers most solo use cases before you'd need to upgrade.
tools.why: A spreadsheet that learned necromancy. Powerful, with a generous free plan, but it takes a few sessions to master.

tools.name: Attio
tools.caption: Every ledger promises it remembers everything about everyone. This one just admits it charges by the memory.
tools.desc: A flexible, data-first CRM with AI research and enrichment built into every plan, including a free tier for up to 3 seats and 50,000 records, or $29/seat/month for Plus.
tools.fact: Unlike most CRMs that gate AI behind the priciest tier, Attio ships AI enrichment on its free plan too, just metered by monthly credits instead of a seat count.
tools.why: A modern CRM with AI on every plan, free included. A strong pick for small parties tracking many quests.

tools.name: Toggl Track
tools.caption: The hourglass could tell you exactly how the day disappeared. It could not, unfortunately, bring any of it back.
tools.desc: Time tracking with AI-assisted categorization; free for up to 5 users.
tools.fact: Free plan supports up to 5 users at no cost, unusually generous for a time tracker.
tools.why: Free for small parties and dead simple to use. The AI is a garnish, not the main course.

tools.name: Luma Dream Machine
tools.caption: The illusion finally understands where the walls are supposed to be, so the dragon stops flying through the castle instead of around it.
tools.desc: AI video generation known for realistic depth, camera movement, and physical space.
tools.fact: Started as a 3D-capture company before pivoting to video, which shows in how well it renders room depth.
tools.why: Video with real depth and camera movement, free to try. Strong, credit-limited.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.caption: The royal painter's guild finally issues its own enchanted brush, trained only on paintings the guild is legally allowed to have painted.
tools.desc: Adobe's AI image and design generator, built into Photoshop, Illustrator, and Express.
tools.fact: Trained specifically on licensed and public-domain content, positioned as safer for commercial use.
tools.why: Commercially safer images inside the Adobe tools you may already rent. Great if you live in Adobe's castle.

tools.name: Leonardo AI
tools.caption: A forge built specifically for turning a game designer's scribbles into armor concept art nobody has to apologize for showing the guild.
tools.desc: AI image generation aimed at game assets, concept art, and stylized illustration.
tools.fact: Its Phoenix model and real-time canvas are popular specifically with game studios for concept art pipelines.
tools.why: Strong for game art and stylized illustration, with free daily credits. A favorite of the concept-art guild.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.caption: The sign painter finally gets an apprentice who remembers the shop's exact colors and lettering every single time, instead of reinventing the crest weekly.
tools.desc: AI image generation built for designers: brand-consistent graphics, icons, and layouts.
tools.fact: One of the only AI image tools that natively outputs scalable SVG files, not just flat images.
tools.why: Brand-consistent graphics, icons, and vectors. The image tool that thinks like a designer.

tools.name: Replit
tools.caption: Ask the apprentice to build you a whole workshop overnight and it does, then hands you a separate bill for the nails.
tools.desc: A browser-based coding environment where Replit Agent can build, run, and deploy a full app from a plain-language prompt, free to start with paid Core at $20/month plus usage-based credits.
tools.fact: The subscription is really just the base fee, actively building with the Agent burns separate usage credits that can add another five to twenty dollars a day on top.
tools.why: Describe an app and Replit Agent builds and hosts it. Easy start, usage costs climb as the app grows.

tools.name: CodeRabbit
tools.caption: Every scroll submitted to the guild now gets read by a very polite rabbit who leaves forty comments before anyone human even looks at it.
tools.desc: An AI code review bot that leaves line-by-line comments on every pull request automatically.
tools.fact: Learns a repo's own conventions over time instead of applying the same generic style rules to every project.
tools.why: Reviews every pull request line by line, free for open source. A tireless second pair of eyes.

tools.name: Magnific
tools.caption: The stock-art warehouse that already had a million paintings decides the fastest way to add a million more is to just paint them itself.
tools.desc: AI image, video, and upscaling studio, renamed from Freepik, bundled with its massive stock photo, vector, and template library.
tools.fact: Freepik renamed itself Magnific in April 2026, after the AI upscaler it bought in 2024, while bootstrapped and reporting $230M in annual recurring revenue.
tools.why: Image generation stapled to a huge stock library with a free tier. A practical one-stop art shop.

tools.name: PixVerse
tools.caption: Text goes in one end, a short moving picture comes out the other, dressed in whatever costume you asked for and none you didn't.
tools.desc: An AI video generator focused on fast text-to-video and image-to-video clips with built-in style templates.
tools.fact: Includes a library of one-click effect templates, aimed at quick social clips rather than long-form production work.
tools.why: Fast text-to-video with style templates and free credits. A capable, cheerful option.

tools.name: Read AI
tools.caption: The court owl remembers every promise made at the round table, which is wonderful for you and terrible for the knight who made it.
tools.desc: An AI meeting assistant that transcribes and summarizes Zoom, Meet, and Teams calls. Free for 5 transcripts a month, Pro from $15/month.
tools.fact: Ask Read searches across your meetings, email, and chat at once, so you can find what was decided without rewatching anything.
tools.why: Solid meeting summaries and cross-app search with a small free tier. A capable scribe, not the cheapest.

tools.name: Tidio
tools.caption: The corner shop that could never afford a night clerk now has one who never sleeps, never complains, and occasionally recommends the wrong potion.
tools.desc: AI chatbot and live chat aimed at small online stores that need support coverage without a support team.
tools.fact: Built specifically for small e-commerce sellers rather than enterprise support desks.
tools.why: Chat and AI support for small shops with a free plan. Exactly sized for the solo storefront.

tools.name: Koala AI
tools.caption: Every forger eventually learns to forge the thing that catches forgers.
tools.desc: AI writer built for SEO-optimized articles, from $9/month.
tools.fact: Runs real-time SERP analysis before drafting, structuring articles to actually compete for a keyword.
tools.why: Cheap, SEO-minded article writer that does its one job well. Not much range outside that job.

tools.name: Poe
tools.caption: One tavern lets you pull up a chair with any oracle in the land, under a single tab, so you can finally compare their prophecies side by side before paying.
tools.desc: Quora's chat platform that gives you access to dozens of different AI models under one subscription.
tools.fact: Lets you compare answers from GPT, Claude, Gemini, and other models side by side in the same place.
tools.why: One subscription, dozens of familiars. Great for sampling the bestiary, though points-based limits run out fast.

tools.name: Kapwing
tools.caption: One workshop now handles the subtitles, the translation, and the dubbing all in the same room, instead of shipping the scroll to three different guilds.
tools.desc: An all-in-one video editor with AI subtitles, translation, and dubbing built alongside normal editing tools.
tools.fact: Handles auto-subtitles in 100+ languages and dubbing in 70+, without leaving the main editor.
tools.why: A friendly online editor with subtitles and dubbing built in, free to start. A great all-rounder.

tools.name: Pika
tools.caption: Quick, stylized illusions that look like a bard's fever dream in the best possible way, gone again before you can quite explain what happened.
tools.desc: An AI video generator focused on quick, stylized clips and creative effects.
tools.fact: Popular for its one-click visual effects library, objects exploding, melting, and transforming.
tools.why: Quick, stylized clips and playful effects with a free tier. More party trick than production line.

tools.name: Sider
tools.caption: A familiar perched on your shoulder whispers summaries of every scroll you open, in the voice of whichever of twenty wizards you prefer today.
tools.desc: A browser sidebar extension that puts GPT, Claude, Gemini, and 20+ other models on any webpage, summarizing pages, chatting with PDFs, and translating without switching tabs.
tools.fact: Started in 2019 as a simple ChatGPT sidebar and has grown into a platform with over 10 million active users.
tools.why: A sidebar that brings twenty-odd models to any webpage. Handy, though you're renting other wizards' spells.

tools.name: Speechify
tools.caption: A bard who will read any scroll aloud, at any speed, forever, and never once complain that your handwriting is terrible.
tools.desc: Reads articles, PDFs, emails, and web pages aloud in natural voices across 60+ languages. Free plan with basic voices, Premium for the human-sounding ones.
tools.fact: Also does voice typing, turns documents into AI podcasts, and has a voice assistant you can ask about what you're reading.
tools.why: Wonderful for listening instead of reading, but the voices worth hearing live behind a pricey Premium tier.

tools.name: AIVA
tools.caption: The court composer never sleeps, never gets writer's block, and never once complains about scoring the same tavern brawl for the fourth time this week.
tools.desc: AI music composition built for scoring original soundtracks, from film cues to game music.
tools.fact: Was recognized as the first AI to be officially registered as a composer with a music rights society.
tools.why: Composes original soundtracks with a free tier. A court composer who works for crumbs.

tools.name: Hark
tools.caption: A squire who carries your whole errand list, books the inn, orders the stew, and asks permission before touching the coin purse. Give it your keys and pray it reads the scroll twice.
tools.desc: Privacy-focused personal AI assistant that books, orders and handles email for you; free to use, with Pro plans at $20 and $100 a month for more usage.
tools.fact: Its Panels feature builds custom mini-apps from a plain description, and they can connect to services like Strava, Spotify and Venmo.
tools.why: Free tier and every feature on every plan make this a generous familiar, but a brand-new squire with your inbox and credit cards is a leap of faith.

tools.name: Lex
tools.caption: A quiet writing tower with no distractions, except the polite ghost who offers to rewrite your paragraph whenever you whisper the summoning word.
tools.desc: A distraction-free AI word processor where you write normally and trigger AI feedback, brainstorming, or rewriting with a typed shortcut instead of a separate chat window.
tools.fact: Style Guides can be trained on your own past writing samples, so its suggestions start sounding like you instead of generic AI.
tools.why: A calm, distraction-free word processor with AI on call. A writer's quiet tower.

tools.name: MyArchitectAI
tools.caption: You hand the sketch to the apprentice architect and get back a fully rendered manor, inside and out, before the real architect finishes their tea.
tools.desc: Generates interior and exterior design renders from a photo or sketch, with a free tier covering 10 renders and 10 edits before $29/month plans kick in.
tools.fact: It renders both interior room redesigns and full exterior architectural concepts from the same tool, most competitors only do one or the other.
tools.why: Interior and exterior renders with free renders to start. A handy sketchbook for home dreamers.

tools.name: Rocket Money
tools.caption: You hand the golem the whole coin purse, and it comes back having quietly canceled three subscriptions you forgot you were paying for.
tools.desc: Tracks spending, subscriptions, and net worth, and can negotiate bills or cancel subscriptions on your behalf.
tools.fact: Will actually call and negotiate a lower bill for you, not just flag that a bill went up.
tools.why: Finds and cancels forgotten subscriptions, free to start. It may pay for itself by slaying one zombie subscription.

tools.name: Teal
tools.caption: Applying to forty castles used to mean forty scrolls in forty drawers. Now there's one ledger, and the ledger judges you quietly.
tools.desc: An AI resume builder with a built-in job tracker for managing multiple applications at once.
tools.fact: Its Job Matcher feature highlights exactly which skills and keywords a resume is missing for a specific job post.
tools.why: Resume builder plus job tracker with a usable free tier. The best overall kit for a job-hunting quest.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.caption: The apprentice read the entire castle blueprint before touching a single brick, which is more than the last three architects did.
tools.desc: Anthropic's AI coding agent that plans, writes, tests, and commits code from your terminal, IDE, desktop app, or browser. Included with Claude Pro from $20/month.
tools.fact: Can work on several tasks in parallel and map an unfamiliar codebase in seconds, without you hand-picking which files it should read.
tools.why: One of the strongest coding agents in the land, included with Claude Pro. No free tier, and it assumes you can read code.

tools.name: Wix
tools.caption: A short conversation with the wizard's apprentice produces a whole working storefront, no incantations required, no scroll of instructions to read first.
tools.desc: A website builder with an AI chat-based setup wizard that generates a starting site from a short conversation.
tools.fact: Its AI assistant asks about your business first, then generates a tailored starting site instead of a generic template.
tools.why: An AI wizard builds you a site from a short chat. Easy and capable, upsells lurk around every corner.

tools.name: GenPage
tools.caption: A scribe who rewrites the guild banner for every traveler who walks through the gate. The free plan gives 100 credits a month, and the Pro tier at $79 removes the 'Made with GenPage' badge.
tools.desc: AI platform that builds personalized landing pages per ad, keyword or visitor intent. Free plan is $0 with 100 credits a month; Pro is $79/month.
tools.fact: The free plan allows unlimited pages and campaigns, with the monthly credits as the real limit.
tools.why: Real free plan and a tidy trick for per-visitor pages, though the best toys (custom domains, API) sit behind the $79 Pro door.

tools.name: Missive
tools.caption: Three scribes finally share one inbox instead of three, and the guild forgets to mention there's a free desk in the back if you know to ask.
tools.desc: A shared team inbox that merges email, chat, and tasks into one thread view, with an unadvertised free plan for up to 3 users and paid plans from $14/user/month.
tools.fact: The free tier isn't listed on the pricing page at all, it only shows up in Missive's own billing documentation.
tools.why: Shared inbox, chat, and tasks in one thread, with a free plan for tiny teams. Practical and underrated.

tools.name: MyFitnessPal
tools.caption: You show the ledger a picture of your dinner and it estimates the damage without making you weigh a single crumb, mercifully.
tools.desc: AI-assisted food logging and calorie tracking, including logging a meal from a photo.
tools.fact: Can estimate a full meal's nutrition breakdown from a single photo instead of manual entry.
tools.why: Photo meal logging and a giant food database with a free tier. Useful, though the best tricks are Premium.

tools.name: Quizlet
tools.caption: The study group golem quizzes you on your own notes at 2 a.m., and somehow remains more patient about it than your actual study group ever was.
tools.desc: AI-assisted flashcards and study tools that generate practice questions from your own notes.
tools.fact: Can turn a pasted set of class notes into a full practice test in seconds.
tools.why: Easy flashcards and practice tests from your notes. The AI is useful, the best bits sit behind Plus.

tools.name: ClickUp Brain
tools.caption: They'd added an oracle to the war table. The war table already had eleven levers too many.
tools.desc: AI layer on ClickUp's project management platform, sold as a paid add-on ($7-9/month) on top of a base plan.
tools.fact: Best for solopreneurs already using ClickUp for task tracking, since per-seat AI pricing math favors a team of one.
tools.why: Smart oracle, cluttered war table. Capable when you find the right lever, but there are a lot of levers.

tools.name: Craft
tools.caption: The parchment was so beautiful nobody noticed three weeks passed and nothing was written on it.
tools.desc: A visually polished notes and document app with AI writing assistance.
tools.fact: Positioned as a more design-forward, visual alternative to Notion.
tools.why: Lovely notes and docs with helpful AI. More polish than raw power.

tools.name: Calendly
tools.caption: The scroll that spares you from ever asking 'does Tuesday work' also books you a meeting at dawn you never wanted.
tools.desc: Scheduling with AI-assisted call routing and no-show reduction.
tools.fact: Can route a booking to the right team member automatically based on the meeting type.
tools.why: The easiest spell in the book: share a link, let the meeting cast itself. Not much magic beyond that, and it doesn't pretend otherwise.

tools.name: Durable
tools.caption: A shop built in sixty seconds looks exactly like a shop, right up until someone tries to open the door.
tools.desc: Generates a full small-business website, copy, images, and booking, in under a minute.
tools.fact: Also auto-generates basic business tools like invoices and a CRM alongside the website itself.
tools.why: A website, CRM, and booking calendar in one quick spell. Not deep, but very fast to stand up.

tools.name: Numerous.ai
tools.caption: Nobody in the guild could explain the spell anymore. Everybody was too afraid to delete it.
tools.desc: AI formulas that live inside Google Sheets and Excel, from $8/month billed yearly.
tools.fact: Lets you write a plain-language instruction as a spreadsheet formula instead of a nested function.
tools.why: A small, cheap spell inside Google Sheets that does one useful thing very well.

tools.name: Fyxer AI
tools.caption: A squire sorts your mail into piles, drafts polite replies, and sits in on your council meetings, all after a seven-day tryout.
tools.desc: An AI email assistant for Gmail and Outlook that triages your inbox into priority categories, drafts replies in your tone, and joins video calls to take notes.
tools.fact: There's no permanent free tier, every plan starts as a 7-day trial before billing kicks in at $30/user/month.
tools.why: Sorts your inbox and drafts replies in your voice, with a free trial. A promising inbox squire.

tools.name: Jamie
tools.caption: No bot walks into the war room. The notes just appear afterward anyway, which raises more questions than it answers.
tools.desc: A bot-free AI notetaker that captures audio locally, in person or online, without a visible bot joining the call.
tools.fact: Runs on European servers and is built GDPR-first, aimed at meetings where a visible recording bot isn't an option.
tools.why: Bot-free notes captured locally, in person or online. Discreet and capable, smaller free allowance.

tools.name: Krisp
tools.caption: A spell of silence falls on the dragon, the blacksmith next door, and the neighbor's dog, but never, tragically, on the meeting itself.
tools.desc: AI noise cancellation, transcription, and meeting notes that work across any calling app. 7-day free trial, then from $8/user/month billed annually.
tools.fact: Removes background noise on both ends of the call, so it can mute the other person's barking dog too.
tools.why: Silences every barking dog on both ends of the call. Excellent at its trick, paid after a short trial.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.caption: You can chain together every tool in the workshop into one very long, very fragile contraption, and it is somehow still faster than doing it by hand.
tools.desc: A framework for building LLM-powered apps and agents, chaining prompts, tools, and memory into one pipeline.
tools.fact: Became such a default starting point for early AI agent projects that its name turned into shorthand for the whole category.
tools.why: Free, open-source plumbing for AI apps. Mighty if you code, a maze of pipes if you don't.

tools.name: PandaDoc
tools.caption: The proposal, the quote, the contract, and the signature line finally live in the same scroll instead of four scrolls chasing each other around the office.
tools.desc: AI-assisted proposals, quotes, contracts, and e-signatures in one document workflow.
tools.fact: Tracks exactly when a recipient opens and scrolls through a document, before they ever sign it.
tools.why: Proposals, quotes, and e-signatures with a free e-sign tier. A tidy deal-closing satchel.

tools.name: ProWritingAid
tools.caption: The editor's quill is built for the long haul, checking a whole novel's worth of parchment instead of just one hasty tavern flyer.
tools.desc: An AI-enhanced grammar and style editor built for long-form writing like novels and manuscripts, not just short-form copy.
tools.fact: Runs dozens of specialized reports, pacing, dialogue tags, sentence-length variation, well beyond a basic grammar check.
tools.why: Deep style and grammar checks for long manuscripts. A novelist's editor with a free tier.

tools.name: AltText.ai
tools.caption: A blind bard is finally told what's on the tapestry, and it took the kingdom this long to think of hiring a narrator.
tools.desc: Generates descriptive alt text for images automatically, plugging into WordPress, Shopify, and other CMSs.
tools.fact: Understands context well enough to describe a product photo differently than an editorial or decorative image.
tools.why: Writes alt text for every image so your site is readable for everyone. Narrow, useful, and kind.

tools.name: Composer
tools.caption: You describe the trading strategy out loud instead of coding the spell yourself, and the market golem quietly runs it exactly as told, for better or worse.
tools.desc: AI-assisted, no-code trading strategy builder that backtests stock and ETF strategies, with a free tier for building and backtesting, or $32/month for live automated execution.
tools.fact: You describe a trading idea in plain language or a visual editor, and it turns that into a fully automated, rebalancing strategy without writing a line of code.
tools.why: Build and backtest trading strategies without code, free to try. Remember: the dice do not care about your backtest.

tools.name: Fitbod
tools.caption: A drill sergeant that actually remembers yesterday's workout and adjusts today's accordingly, instead of just yelling the same routine forever.
tools.desc: AI-personalized strength training plans that adapt each workout based on what you did last time.
tools.fact: Adjusts the next workout's exercises and volume based on your recovery and performance in the last session.
tools.why: Adapts each workout to how you actually trained. A helpful squire for the gym, paid after a few sessions.

tools.name: Virtual Staging AI
tools.caption: An empty room in the listing photo gets furnished by illusion instead of an actual moving cart, and the buyer never has to know which parts are real.
tools.desc: Digitally furnishes an empty listing photo with AI-generated furniture instead of hiring a staging company.
tools.fact: Turns an empty room photo into a fully furnished one in under a minute, at a fraction of physical staging cost.
tools.why: Furnishes empty rooms for a fraction of real staging. Fast and cheap per photo.

tools.name: You.com
tools.caption: A tavern that lets you pick which bard tells the story. The story changes more than you'd like depending who's holding the lute.
tools.desc: An AI search engine that lets you choose which underlying model answers your query.
tools.fact: Offers over 30 specialized AI agents built for different tasks like research, writing, and coding.
tools.why: Lets you pick which model answers. Flexible, but outshone by the bigger search familiars.

tools.name: Epique AI
tools.caption: The listing scroll writes itself the moment the agent walks through the door, along with the follow-up letters nobody wanted to draft at midnight.
tools.desc: An AI platform built specifically for real estate agents: listing descriptions, client emails, and social posts.
tools.fact: Generates MLS-ready listing copy alongside the buyer and seller emails an agent needs for the same transaction.
tools.why: AI listing descriptions and emails built for real estate agents. Narrow, handy, affordable.

tools.name: GPTZero
tools.caption: The forgery inspector is right often enough to keep the job and wrong often enough to ruin someone's afternoon.
tools.desc: One of the first widely-used AI-text detectors, aimed at teachers and publishers checking for AI-written content.
tools.fact: Was originally built by a Princeton student before growing into one of the most recognized names in AI detection.
tools.why: Easy and free to start, beloved by teachers. Like every AI detector, it can accuse an innocent scroll.

tools.name: Rill Browser
tools.caption: The party's wizard finally got a tavern of their own: Claude and Codex pull up chairs beside you while you browse. The catch is you must already hold a guild membership, and only Apple silicon Macs may enter.
tools.desc: A free macOS browser (beta) where Claude Code and Codex work beside you, running on your existing plan with no new subscription or API keys.
tools.fact: Browsing works without any agent, and its agent features need Claude Code 2.1.261 or later or Codex CLI 0.144.4 or later.
tools.why: Free to enter and lets your existing familiars ride along, but it is a 0.1 beta, Apple-silicon-only, and useless without a Claude or Codex plan.

tools.name: Bonsai
tools.caption: The dragon's hoard was never the problem. Getting the dragon to actually pay the invoice was.
tools.desc: Contracts, invoicing, and scheduling for freelancers; Essentials tier is the sweet spot.
tools.fact: Bundles contracts, invoicing, and scheduling into one dashboard built specifically for freelancers.
tools.why: Contracts, invoices, and scheduling for freelancers in one tidy pouch. Dependable, not flashy.

tools.name: HeyGen
tools.caption: The talking portrait finally learns to move its mouth in the right language, no matter which tongue the visitor speaks.
tools.desc: AI avatar video generation with strong lip-sync and video translation.
tools.fact: Can take a video in English and dub it into dozens of languages while matching the speaker's lips to the new language.
tools.why: The best lip-sync and video translation in town. Avatar magic that costs real gold.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.caption: A wizard's apprentice builds you a whole working castle from a sketch on a napkin, in the time it takes to finish your ale.
tools.desc: A browser-based AI app builder built for fast, full-stack prototyping with no local setup.
tools.fact: Its daily token allowance resets every 24 hours, keeping it usable for ongoing experimentation.
tools.why: Spins up full-stack apps in the browser. Fun and fast, but tokens drain quickly once the bugs start.

tools.name: Figma Make
tools.caption: The illusionist finally learned to conjure with the kingdom's official crest instead of whatever font he felt like that morning.
tools.desc: Figma's prompt-to-prototype tool that generates working, code-backed designs you can keep editing visually on the canvas.
tools.fact: Make kits pull in your real component library and npm packages, so generated screens use your design system instead of generic boxes.
tools.why: Prompt-to-prototype that respects your real design system. Great inside Figma, gated by its plans.

tools.name: Grok
tools.caption: An oracle that reads the town gossip board before answering anything will eventually tell you the gossip board is correct.
tools.desc: xAI's chatbot, built into X (formerly Twitter) with real-time access to what's trending on the platform.
tools.fact: Grok Imagine can generate images and short videos from the same chat window.
tools.why: Sharp and plugged into X's live firehose, but the best features sit behind paid tiers and its chaotic alignment is a feature, apparently.

tools.name: Higgsfield
tools.caption: The camera in this illusion sweeps and swoops like a bard telling the story of a battle they definitely weren't at, and somehow it still looks convincing.
tools.desc: An AI video generation platform built around cinematic camera movement and stylized motion presets.
tools.fact: Offers a library of named camera-move presets, so a specific dramatic zoom or pan can be applied with one click instead of a prompt.
tools.why: Cinematic camera moves on demand. Gorgeous presets, credit-hungry.

tools.name: Kagi
tools.caption: One well in the village charges a toll and, unlike every free well, doesn't sell your bucket to advertisers.
tools.desc: A paid, ad-free search engine with AI features layered on top and no ads or tracking to fund it.
tools.fact: Lets you manually boost or block specific websites from ever appearing in your results again.
tools.why: Ad-free search you pay for, which is refreshing and also, well, paying for search. Worth it for the devoted.

tools.name: Genspark
tools.caption: The Super Agent researches the quest, builds the slide deck, and calls the innkeeper for you. It only asks that you keep feeding it credits.
tools.desc: An all-in-one AI workspace built around a Super Agent that can research, build slide decks, analyze data, and make calls from a single dashboard.
tools.fact: Basic AI chat and image generation run on zero credits through the end of 2026, a temporary perk buried in the pricing fine print.
tools.why: A Super Agent that researches and builds decks for you. Impressive when it works, credit-hungry when it doesn't.

tools.name: Gumloop
tools.caption: Draw the contraption on a canvas, connect the gears, and a little team of goblin agents runs every lever at once.
tools.desc: A no-code AI automation platform where you build workflows on a visual canvas, chaining triggers, logic, integrations, and AI actions including web scraping and document parsing.
tools.fact: It can run multiple AI sub-agents in parallel within a single workflow, each handling a different task at the same time.
tools.why: A friendly visual canvas for AI automations. Easier than Zapier for AI-heavy flows, younger and less proven.

tools.name: Async
tools.caption: The traveling podcast caravan got a new name and a bigger stage. Same troupe, same prices, more scenery.
tools.desc: A browser-based podcast and video studio combining remote recording, multi-track editing, AI noise cleanup, and voice cloning in one platform.
tools.fact: Rebranded from Podcastle to Async in February 2026 as the platform expanded from podcasting into video and code-enabled workflows, existing accounts and pricing carried over unchanged.
tools.why: Recording, editing, and AI cleanup in the browser with a free tier. A whole studio in one tab.

tools.name: Ocoya
tools.caption: The crier's scroll now writes its own announcements too, which means the town hears the same enthusiastic tone in every single square.
tools.desc: AI social media scheduling and caption generation across 30+ platforms, with a free tier to start and paid plans from $19/month.
tools.fact: It bundles AI copywriting directly into the scheduling calendar, so captions, hashtags, and post variations get generated on the same screen where you queue the post.
tools.why: AI captions and scheduling across 30+ platforms with a free tier. Broad reach, lighter polish.

tools.name: Uizard
tools.caption: A rough sketch on a napkin turns into a working mockup of the whole guildhall before the ale's even gone flat.
tools.desc: An AI tool that turns rough sketches or text prompts into clickable app and website mockups.
tools.fact: Can convert a photo of a hand-drawn wireframe into an editable digital design.
tools.why: Turns sketches into clickable mockups with a free tier. Friendly for non-designers.

tools.name: Soundraw
tools.caption: Describe the mood of the scene and a full royalty-free score appears, custom built and never once haggled over with a guild musician.
tools.desc: Generates royalty-free AI music customized by mood, genre, and length for videos and content.
tools.fact: Lets you edit the structure of a generated track, swapping sections in and out, instead of taking it as-is.
tools.why: Royalty-free music shaped by mood and length. A dependable background bard.

tools.name: Loom
tools.caption: The crystal ball let him watch the whole meeting whenever he wanted. He wanted, apparently, never.
tools.desc: Async video messaging with AI transcripts and summaries; free tier caps videos at 5 minutes.
tools.fact: Auto-generates a written summary and action items from any recorded video.
tools.why: Effortless to record and share, docked because the free tier caps how long and how many videos you get.

tools.name: Suno
tools.caption: The bard could write a note perfect ballad about anything in nine seconds. Nobody could hum it back nine seconds later.
tools.desc: AI music generation that turns a text prompt into a full song with vocals and structure, from $8/month billed yearly.
tools.fact: Its latest model closes most of the uncanny valley in AI vocals, they sound like a real singer now.
tools.why: Writes full songs with vocals from a sentence, and the free tier is fun. Commercial rights require gold.

tools.name: Murf AI
tools.caption: A narrator's voice, studio-polished and tireless, reads your scroll aloud without ever needing a throat lozenge.
tools.desc: AI voiceover generation aimed at studio-quality narration for videos and presentations.
tools.fact: Includes a built-in voice changer that converts your own recorded voice into polished narration.
tools.why: Polished voiceovers for videos and slides. Easy and reliable, outclassed by ElevenLabs on range.

tools.name: Cleanvoice
tools.caption: Every stray cough, um, and awkward pause gets quietly swept off the recording, and the bard never has to know how many there really were.
tools.desc: Automated podcast audio cleanup that strips filler words, breaths, stutters, and long pauses from a raw recording.
tools.fact: Its filler-word detection works across multiple languages, not just English, and can shorten long dead-air pauses automatically.
tools.why: Strips filler words and stutters from raw audio. Narrow, effective, mostly paid.

tools.name: Grain
tools.caption: The council's driest three-hour meeting gets cut down to the one moment everyone actually needed to see, mercifully.
tools.desc: AI meeting recording built around turning call moments into shareable video clips.
tools.fact: Designed so sales and customer teams can clip a 30-second moment from a call instead of the whole recording.
tools.why: Turns call moments into shareable clips. Nice for sales and research calls, narrower than the big notetakers.

tools.name: Pitch
tools.caption: Three bards write the same ballad on the same page at once, without shoving. Ambitious, for a tavern this small.
tools.desc: A collaborative presentation tool built for teams, with real-time multiplayer editing and AI slide generation, free to start with paid plans from around $11/seat/month.
tools.fact: It was built by former Wunderlist founders specifically to fix the parts of pitch decks that get stuck in email attachments and version-numbered filenames.
tools.why: Collaborative decks with AI slides and a free tier. Great for teams, fine for one.

tools.name: Plus AI
tools.caption: The slide-deck spell now lives inside the same scroll-writing tool the guild already uses, instead of demanding you learn an entirely new spellbook.
tools.desc: An AI slide generator that works as an add-on directly inside Google Slides and PowerPoint.
tools.fact: Builds and edits decks inside the presentation software you already use, instead of a separate app to export from.
tools.why: Generates slides right inside Google Slides and PowerPoint. Convenient, paid after the trial.

tools.name: Vanna AI
tools.caption: Instead of hiring one more scribe who speaks fluent database, you teach the golem to translate for you, and it never once asks for a raise.
tools.desc: An open-source framework for building your own text-to-SQL assistant on top of your database.
tools.fact: Because it's open-source, developers can self-host it and fine-tune it on their own schema instead of using a black box.
tools.why: Open-source text-to-SQL you build yourself. Free and flexible, if you can build it.

tools.name: Looka
tools.caption: A new tavern picks its crest, its banner, and its signage all from the same enchanted stamp, in an afternoon instead of a season.
tools.desc: An AI logo and brand identity generator aimed at new small businesses.
tools.fact: Generates a full brand kit, logo, colors, fonts, and social templates, from a single questionnaire.
tools.why: Logo and brand kit in minutes, free to design. You pay only when you download, which is fair.

tools.name: Sanebox
tools.caption: A postmaster has been quietly sorting the kingdom's junk mail into neat piles since before anyone called it magic, and still does.
tools.desc: An inbox filtering tool that quietly sorts newsletters, notifications, and noise out of your main inbox using folder rules instead of AI chat, from $7/month for one account.
tools.fact: It's been running the same folder-based filtering approach since 2010, one of the few tools on this entire list that predates the AI boom by over a decade.
tools.why: Quietly sweeps newsletters and noise out of your inbox. Simple, effective, and paid after the trial.

tools.name: Simplified
tools.caption: One wagon carries the paint, the quill, the puppet stage, and the town crier's bell. Not the best of any, but one wagon is easier to pull.
tools.desc: A bundled marketing suite combining a no-code design editor, AI writer, video editor, and social scheduler in one subscription, aimed at small teams that don't want five separate tools.
tools.fact: The free plan's AI writing credits are a one-time allotment of about 5,000 words that never renews, everything after that requires upgrading.
tools.why: Design, writing, video, and scheduling in one bundle. Jack of many trades, master of few.

tools.name: Calm
tools.caption: The sleep potion now studies your sleeping habits before brewing itself, which feels less like magic and more like being watched while you nap.
tools.desc: A meditation and sleep app with AI-personalized content recommendations.
tools.fact: Tailors its daily meditation and sleep content suggestions to your own usage patterns over time.
tools.why: Soothing, easy, and polished. The AI is a light touch on a meditation app most people use for the rain sounds.

tools.name: Cleo
tools.caption: The money advisor finally has a sense of humor about your spending, which somehow stings more than a stern lecture ever did.
tools.desc: A conversational AI budgeting assistant built to make money management approachable, aimed at younger users.
tools.fact: Delivers budgeting nudges through a chat interface with personality, rather than a traditional dashboard.
tools.why: A sassy budgeting chatbot that roasts your spending. Fun and approachable, light on depth.

tools.name: HubSpot Free CRM
tools.caption: The first vine is always free. Nobody mentions the garden was built to grow toward a gate you'll pay to open.
tools.desc: Free CRM tier is genuinely solid; AI features (Breeze) are rate-limited or paid.
tools.fact: The free CRM tier has no user cap or expiration date, unusual among free CRM offers.
tools.why: The free tier is a sturdy keep. The AI wing is real but locked behind a toll gate that gets pricier every floor.

tools.name: Make
tools.caption: The engine had six hundred gears and one of them was a mouse on a wheel. Nobody remembered which.
tools.desc: Visual automation platform and a direct alternative to Zapier; credit-based pricing.
tools.fact: Its canvas-style builder shows an entire automation, branches and all, on one screen.
tools.why: A cheaper, more flexible Zapier with a steeper learning curve. Strong value if you're willing to read the spellbook.

tools.name: Monarch Money
tools.caption: One dashboard finally shows the whole treasury at once instead of forty scrolls in forty different vaults.
tools.desc: A budgeting and financial tracking app that gives a single clear view of spending, saving, and net worth.
tools.fact: Built to give a full household financial picture in one dashboard, not just a single account view.
tools.why: Clear, complete money tracking for couples and households. Paid, but many say worth it.

tools.name: Copilot Money
tools.caption: The ledger finally sorts your coin purse by itself, and it's disturbingly good at recognizing exactly where the gold keeps vanishing to.
tools.desc: AI-powered personal budgeting and net-worth tracking with automatic transaction categorization.
tools.fact: Its AI learns your individual spending patterns over time instead of relying on generic category rules.
tools.why: A beautiful budgeting app with smart categorization. Paid after the trial, Apple-first.

tools.name: RemodelAI
tools.caption: One photograph of a shabby room goes in, a fully furnished, suspiciously flattering version comes out, and the actual furniture still has to be bought separately.
tools.desc: Photorealistic room redesigns from a single photo, plus exterior, virtual staging, and paint-color tools.
tools.fact: Offers 30+ distinct design styles and lets you try several before committing to a real renovation.
tools.why: Photoreal redesigns, staging, and paint previews. Capable, mostly paid.

tools.name: Interior AI
tools.caption: Describe the tavern you want and the room redecorates itself on parchment before the carpenter's even been summoned.
tools.desc: Generates fully styled interior spaces from a room photo or a plain-language description.
tools.fact: Can also auto-generate a matching mood board alongside the redesigned room, not just a single image.
tools.why: Restyles a room from one photo. Fun and quick, light on free tries.

tools.name: Rezi
tools.caption: A scribe drafts you a résumé scroll built to slip past the gatekeeper golem, then charges you once and considers the friendship over.
tools.desc: An ATS-safe AI resume builder aimed specifically at tech job seekers, sold as a lifetime plan.
tools.fact: Built its formatting specifically to survive strict ATS parsing rather than to look good to a human first.
tools.why: ATS-safe resumes with a lifetime plan option. Focused and fair, but narrow.

tools.name: Anara
tools.caption: Every other oracle answers from the void. This one insists on flipping to the exact page the answer came from.
tools.desc: An AI research assistant for reading, summarizing, and citing academic papers, with direct search across PubMed, arXiv, and JSTOR.
tools.fact: Rebranded from Unriddle AI in 2025 and is now used by more than 3 million researchers, including people at Stanford, MIT, and Johns Hopkins.
tools.why: Cites the exact passage in your own documents. Strong scholar, steeper price than the free alternatives.

tools.name: Gamma
tools.caption: The banners were beautiful. Nobody could recall afterward what the parade had actually been for.
